context: Request: completed Capital Markets offerings whose proceeds were earmarked primarily for general corporate purposes, with the documents showing the earmark and the closing. Rubric: 1045-00001 (Belmont Ridge Bank subordinated notes) as qualifying, its use-of-proceeds document (final offering memorandum) and one of its closing documents (indenture, purchase agreement, closing funds-flow memorandum or pricing-confirmation e-mail), and a precision criterion permitting only 1045-00001 and 1014-00001; 1009-00001 (Skybridge convertible-note bridge) is outside the set.

runs.failure_point: It cited a client closing letter, not the executed or funds-flow closing papers shown in its own listing, as closing proof for the qualifying matter, and wrote a convertible-note bridge financing as a qualifying offering.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: Reviews asked for use-of-proceeds sections ([80]) and for closing evidence of two picked matters ([88]), but none said the client closing letter was weak proof or named the indenture or funds-flow papers; the agent re-read the same letter.
first_error.why: For the subordinated-notes matter it opened only the offering memorandum and the client closing letter, leaving out the indenture, closing funds-flow memorandum and pricing-confirmation e-mail shown in its own listing at [49]-[50], so the answer's closing proof is the letter.

other_errors.critic_note: No review questioned the bridge financing; the check-stage reviews ([123], [133]) told the agent to leave the qualifying set unchanged unless a matter's own documents failed.
other_errors.why: The answer lists a privately placed convertible-note bridge financing, sold under a note purchase agreement, as a qualifying completed offering (evidence seen at [61]-[93]).

divergence: Mixed (T1, T2 pass; T0 fails). All three runs surfaced and screened the subordinated-notes matter among a dozen offering candidates. They split at screening: T1 read that matter's cross-receipt, indenture and funds flow on its own initiative, and T2 did so after its screening review said the only closing proof seen was a draft regulatory notice; T0 opened only the offering memorandum and a client closing letter, its reviews never questioned that letter, and the answer cited it as closing proof. T0 also wrote a convertible-note bridge financing as qualifying, which no review questioned; T2 read the same deal's note purchase agreement and left it out, and T1 never treated it as a candidate. Agent-declared stages (T1 batched scan and two screening stages, T2 background scan) and label notes played no part in the split; the one label note followed was T2's switch to folder listing.
